title: Figma Make Guidelines: guidelines.md and the Context-Overload Warning
content:
# Add Guidelines to Figma Make

Guidelines are the baseline (non-kit) mechanism for constraining Figma Make generation. They "help Make generate better prototypes by providing instructions on coding behavior, personality, and style context usage."

## Method 1 — manual

Write directly in guidelines.md, or upload existing markdown:
- **Writing in Make:** Code > Guidelines folder > edit guidelines.md
- **Uploading:** drag .md files into the Guidelines folder; multiple files supported

Additional guidelines folders and files can be added by right-clicking the guidelines folder and choosing Create file or Create folder. This makes the mechanism structurally comparable to Lovable's .lovable/rules/ directory and Replit's .agents/skills/ tree — a nested markdown knowledge tree the agent consults.

## Method 2 — AI-generated

"Prompt Figma Make to analyze your npm packages and library styles and write comprehensive guidelines for you." Uses AI credits, may take several minutes. Make generates one or more markdown files covering components, styles, tokens, and general design system rules, which you then review and refine with specific use cases and edge cases.

This auto-generation path is a meaningful differentiator: rather than requiring design system teams to hand-author agent documentation, Make reads the package's component surface and the library's styles and drafts the guidelines itself, leaving humans to correct and add edge cases.

## Template structure

- General guidelines (layout, code practices)
- Design system guidelines (fonts, spacing, component rules)
- Component-specific details with usage and variants

## The key limitation, verbatim

**"More context isn't always better. It can confuse the LLM."**

Figma is explicitly warning against dumping an entire design system documentation site into guidelines. This is worth flagging to practitioners who assume more knowledge files means better adherence — and it sits in direct tension with the instinct to give an agent everything.

The convergent industry lesson across vendors: a thin always-loaded layer plus progressively-disclosed detail beats one large knowledge dump. Replit splits always-on custom instructions from on-demand skills for the same reason; Lovable splits the auto-generated schema from the hand-authored system.md.
